intro: A wet room is one of the most practical and stylish bathroom upgrades you can make, and in Gorebridge it's becoming an increasingly popular choice for homeowners looking to add real value to their property. That might sound like a significant outlay, but a well-installed wet room done by someone who understands the specific demands of local properties will last decades and comfortably add more than its cost to your home's value.
localContext: Gorebridge has a genuinely mixed housing stock, and that variety matters when you're planning a wet room. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up a good portion of the town present particular challenges — walls can be uneven, floors may not be level, and older construction methods mean you can't always assume what you'll find once work begins. These properties often need more preparation work before a wet room can be properly installed, which is reflected in the cost. Modern estates in Gorebridge tend to be more straightforward, with more predictable construction and easier access to pipework and drainage. One factor worth bearing in mind across all property types is that Gorebridge sits in a moderately hard water area. This means limescale can gradually build up on shower screens, fittings, and drains, so specifying fittings with easy-clean or hard water resistant finishes is a sensible investment from the outset rather than an afterthought.
serviceDetail: The installation process for a wet room typically unfolds over several days, though more complex projects in older Gorebridge properties can run to a week or more. The first stage is a thorough survey of the existing bathroom — checking the condition of the subfloor, assessing drainage options, and identifying where waterproofing membranes need to go. This survey stage is genuinely important and shouldn't be rushed, particularly in stone-built homes where the floor construction may be unconventional. Once the existing suite is stripped out, any subfloor repairs or levelling work is carried out before the tanking system is applied. Tanking — the continuous waterproof membrane that covers walls and floor — is the most critical part of the whole job. Done properly, it ensures the room stays watertight for many years. The floor is then built up with a fall to the drain, which ensures water runs away cleanly rather than pooling. After the waterproofing is signed off, tiling can begin. Finally, the shower plumbing, screen if required, sanitaryware, and fittings are installed and tested. A good installer will also check that your hot water system can deliver adequate flow and pressure to the shower — an underperforming boiler or cylinder is worth knowing about before the tiles go on.
pricing: In Gorebridge, a straightforward wet room in a modern property with a standard-sized bathroom will typically sit toward the lower end of the £6,000 to £12,000 range. Where costs rise is in older or period properties where preparation work is more involved — levelling uneven floors, repairing original joists, or dealing with unexpected damp. The choice of materials makes a meaningful difference too: mid-range porcelain tiles and decent fittings are included in most quotes, but natural stone, designer sanitaryware, or underfloor heating will push the figure higher. Always ensure your quote includes full tanking, waste installation, and all building work — not just the cosmetic finish.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Gorebridge well isn't just about convenience. Someone who has worked in the area before will have encountered the quirks of local stone-built properties and period cottages first-hand, and won't be surprised by what they find. They'll also understand the importance of getting work right in a smaller town where reputation genuinely matters — word travels fast in a community of around 12,000 people. Local tradespeople are also easier to get back if something needs attention down the line, which for a job as detailed as a wet room installation is worth factoring into your decision.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built property in Gorebridge?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires more preparation than a modern home. Older Gorebridge properties often have uneven floors, solid walls, and non-standard construction that needs addressing before any waterproofing goes in. A good installer will survey thoroughly first and be upfront about any additional work needed. Done properly, these homes can make excellent wet rooms.

faqs.q: How does hard water in Gorebridge affect a wet room long-term?
faqs.a: Gorebridge's moderately hard water supply means limescale will accumulate on fittings, drains, and any glass screen over time. It's worth specifying hard water resistant coatings on screens and easy-clean fittings from the start. Regular use of an appropriate descaler will keep things looking good and extend the life of your fittings significantly.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Gorebridge?
faqs.a: Most installations in newer Gorebridge properties take around four to five days. Older stone-built or period homes can take longer — up to a week or more — if the subfloor needs significant work or there are damp issues to address. Your installer should give you a realistic timeframe after surveying the space, not before.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a wet room in Gorebridge?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. Converting an existing bathroom into a wet room is classed as permitted development. However, if your Gorebridge home is a listed building or sits within a conservation area, it's worth checking with Midlothian Council before work begins. Your installer should be able to advise, but the final responsibility rests with you as the homeowner.
